html:
The last Byzantine emperor, who reigned from 1449 until he died defending Constantinople against the Ottomans on 29 May 1453.

A younger son of Manuel II, he first ruled part of the Despotate of the Morea from Mistra. He repaired the Hexamilion wall and raided into central Greece, until Murad II broke through the wall in 1446.

He became emperor after his brother John VIII died. Hoping for Western help, he had the church union of Florence proclaimed in Hagia Sophia in December 1452, which angered many of his people. Help came only in small numbers, such as the Genoese soldiers of Giovanni Giustiniani.

During the final assault he threw off his imperial insignia and died fighting near the walls. His body was never surely found. Greek legend later told of a "marble emperor" who would one day wake and retake the city.
